An iron lung is a large, horizontal cylinder that acts as a mechanical respirator to help a person breathe when their muscle control is lost or overwhelmed.

How it Works

The device uses negative pressure ventilation. By periodically decreasing and increasing the air pressure inside the sealed tank, it forces the patient's chest to expand and contract, drawing air into and out of the lungs.

Historical Context

  • Polio Epidemic: It was most famously used during the mid-20th century to treat polio victims whose breathing muscles were paralyzed.
  • Obsolescence: While mostly replaced by modern positive-pressure ventilators and intubation, a few individuals still use them today due to specific medical needs or personal preference.

The movie Iron Lung is a science fiction horror film that was released in theaters on January 30, 2026. It is the feature directorial debut of Mark "Markiplier" Fischbach, who also wrote, financed, and stars in the film.

Based on the 2022 indie horror game by David Szymanski, the movie has become a significant box-office hit, grossing over $37 million within its first two weeks.

Plot & Setting

The story takes place in a post-apocalyptic future following an event called "The Quiet Rapture," during which every star and habitable planet in the universe mysteriously vanished. The remnants of humanity live on decaying space stations.

  • The Mission: A convict named Simon (played by Markiplier) is promised freedom if he successfully pilots a small, rusted submarine through an ocean of human blood discovered on a desolate moon (AT-5).
  • The Submarine: The titular "Iron Lung" is a claustrophobic vessel that is welded shut from the outside. Because of the immense pressure, there are no windows; the pilot must navigate using only a still camera, basic instruments, and a map.
  • The Conflict: As Simon descends into the depths to photograph anomalies, he encounters evidence that he is not alone in the blood.

Key Details

  • Cast: Alongside Markiplier, the film features Caroline Rose Kaplan (as Ava), Troy Baker, and a cameo by Seán "Jacksepticeye" McLoughlin.
  • Blood Record: Markiplier claimed during production that the film features the most "fake blood" ever used in a movie, aiming to break world records.
  • Theatrical Release: The film saw a wide release in North America through major chains like AMC and Regal, as well as international screenings in the UK and Australia.

Since you're interested in DIY and electronics, you might find the "grungy" aesthetic of the submarine particularly cool—Markiplier famously focused on practical effects and a "lo-fi" tech feel to replicate the game's atmosphere.
